principles: Do not optimize for the sake of optimization.
drivers: Prevent stale or mixed artifacts from polluting formal unlock proof.
Keep Lattice CLI non-authority for local baseline proof.
Preserve the Authority Server boundary for Production Safety.

options.name: A: Add a narrow formal root invariant inside existing suite aggregation
pros: Directly addresses the pollution failure mode.
Keeps existing artifactsRoot and evaluator flow.
Avoids adding a new capability layer or broad runner rewrite.
cons: Does not add explicit reportFiles support.
Requires tests to cover all-files invariants, not just accepted reports.

options.name: B: Add reportFiles/reportRoot selection support now
pros: Would allow exact file selection for future flows.
Could reduce dependence on directory hygiene.
cons: Broader API surface than needed for this correctness issue.
More risk of arbitrary optimization and new edge cases.

options.name: C: Documentation-only clean-root rule
cons: Does not make the invariant mechanically enforceable.
Would leave the same class of false PASS risk to manual discipline.

chosen: A: Add a narrow formal root invariant inside existing suite aggregation
rationale: Choose the narrow invariant because the real correctness issue is polluted final PASS proof roots. This makes the existing L2/L3 formal path fail closed without expanding API shape or claiming Authority.

preMortem.scenario: The guard blocks valid historical artifacts outside the selected clean root.
preMortem.trigger: The implementation scans the parent unlock directory instead of the supplied artifactsRoot/layer directory.
preMortem.consequence: Fresh unlock runs become unusable when audit history exists.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep the scan scoped to the selected artifactsRoot and add negative coverage for outside-root history not polluting the current suite.

preMortem.scenario: The guard accidentally unlocks Production Safety or treats host review as Authority.
preMortem.trigger: The implementation shares formal evaluator code with production-safety without preserving locked Authority fields.
preMortem.consequence: Local CLI evidence could be overclaimed as production authority.
preMortem.mitigation: Limit formal root invariant authorization to Engineering and Loop Engineering, assert receiptVerified/productionDone/fullAuthorityDone remain false.

preMortem.scenario: Mixed suiteRunId artifacts are rejected but not surfaced clearly.
preMortem.trigger: The guard only adds a generic blocked reason.
preMortem.consequence: Auditors cannot tell whether the failure is stale, mixed, local-only, or claimTarget mismatch.
preMortem.mitigation: Emit explicit blocked reasons for root invariant fields and assert test output mentions suiteRunId/claimTarget/materialHash/localOnly as applicable.
